summary: @ornikar/webpack-config@12.0.3 ships an obfuscated install-time dropper that downloads Bun and executes an opaque payload
details: The package declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`, which runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs itself is obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style `_0xNNNN` identifiers and per-function property-name maps hiding strings such as `ldd`, `/etc/os-release`, `Alpine`, `bun`, and the Bun release URL). It downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods the binary 0o755, and invokes `execFileSync(bunBinary, [math_init.js], {stdio:'inherit'})`. The sibling `math_init.js` is a 727,680-byte heavily obfuscated JavaScript blob (rotating string/opcode array via a `WV8StW` shift function, `_0xNNNN` identifiers, single-line collapsed logic) with no readable relationship to a webpack configuration package. `package.json` declares `main: index.js`, but that file is absent from the tarball — the only code executed by installing this version is the dropper chain. The runtime is fetched from its official project source, but Bun is being used to execute an opaque, obfuscated in-tarball payload rather than any documented package code, which is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern rather than a legitimate runtime install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
